validity.recommendation: No change to existence/classification. P5521 is a real, actively-progressing project: a ~828-830 km gas transmission bridge from the Amur Gas Processing Plant at Svobodny (Amur Oblast), through Birobidzhan (Jewish AO), to a tie-in with the Sakhalin-Khabarovsk-Vladivostok trunk near Khabarovsk, built as Stage 1 of Gazprom's 'Eastern Gas Supply System' (Vostochnaya sistema gazosnabzheniya, VSG). Independently corroborated by interfax.ru (national wire, quoting Gazprom's own annual-report language), the Khabarovsk Krai/Minenergo official statement via dfo.gov.ru, the general contractor Gazstroyprom's own project page (gsprom.ru), neftegaz.ru's technical-library system overview, and construction-progress reporting from portamur.ru (May 2026, 75% built) and akm.ru (Gazprom press-service mirror). See the duplicate, spec, and attribution concerns below for the caveats.
validity.researcher_notes: Read to exhaustion: interfax.ru/business/951688 (whole-VSG announcement article naming this segment specifically, 830 km, pressure spec, fuel-source language), gsprom.ru/projects/gas-trunklines/ (contractor's own project card, 828 km exact), dfo.gov.ru/press/news_DV/7942/ (27-May-2025 official Minenergo statement, 828 km, 2027 target), neftegaz.ru tech-library 830816 (VSG system overview, separates system-wide 'Характеристики проекта ВСГ' from Stage-1-specific 'перемычка' facts -- the source of the aggregate-vs-segment issues below), neftegaz.ru news 889825, akm.ru (Gazprom press-release mirror, April 2025, 1420mm/K70/150atm pipe spec + 356km progress), tek-all.ru (23-Apr-2026 independent overview, corroborates 1420mm diameter but gives a conflicting 9.8 MPa pressure figure), portamur.ru (03-May-2026, 75% built / 754 of 828 km), finance.rambler.ru (26-Jun-2026, Miller AGM commissioning announcement), prokhab.ru via Wayback (27-Oct-2022, dated dispatch confirming April-2022 presidential decision), energypolicy.ru via Wayback (2024 academic analysis of VSG spatial development). No evidence found anywhere describing a different, separate project at this location -- all Russian-language coverage converges on one continuous corridor and construction effort.

validity.recommendation: Adjudicate P5521 against P3208 ('Power of Siberia Gas Pipeline' / 'Phase I Expansion' segment, Blagoveshchensk->Khabarovsk Krai, 620 km, 32 bcm/y, status=cancelled). A separate shard for P3208 staged in this same batch (rows/P3208.json) independently reached the identical conclusion from the other direction: both rows track the same physical corridor -- a connector linking the Power of Siberia (Chayanda-sourced) system to the Sakhalin-Khabarovsk-Vladivostok (Sakhalin-sourced) system across Amur Oblast, the Jewish Autonomous Oblast, and Khabarovsk Krai. energypolicy.ru's 2024 academic account explains the lineage: a Belogorsk-Birobidzhan-Khabarovsk extension was part of Power of Siberia-1's ORIGINAL design (when PoS-1 was to run Chayanda->Vladivostok with an LNG plant there); it was shelved ('otoshel na vtoroy plan') once Gazprom instead routed China-bound gas directly via Blagoveshchensk (the trunk actually built, 2019) -- that shelved concept is very likely GEM's P3208. The SAME corridor was revived in 2022 (Presidential decision, April 2022, per prokhab.ru) under the name 'MG Belogorsk-Khabarovsk' (828-830 km, matching P5521 almost exactly) as VSG Stage 1, formally listed in the Russian government's 16-Nov-2024 decree No. 3302-r alongside Power of Siberia-2. Recommendation: either (a) merge/supersede P3208 into P5521 (the revived project inherits the corridor and P3208 becomes a historical alias), or (b) if GEM's convention is to keep the shelved first-generation concept as its own row, add an explicit note on P3208 that it is the pre-2022 discontinued precursor now tracked live as P5521, and drop or caveat P3208's own 620 km / 32 bcm/y figures -- no source (for either the original or revived concept) supports those numbers; every dated source gives ~800-830 km for this corridor, never 620 km.
validity.researcher_notes: Corroborated independently in this session via interfax.ru, dfo.gov.ru, neftegaz.ru, energypolicy.ru (Wayback), and prokhab.ru (Wayback) -- all naming 'Belogorsk-Khabarovsk' specifically at 828-830 km, never Blagoveshchensk-Khabarovsk at 620 km. Not proposing a mechanical merge myself (that is a database-structure decision for Baird), only staging the finding and cross-referencing the sibling shard so it is not lost.

validity.recommendation: Capacity=28.00 bcm/y is a SYSTEM-wide aggregate figure for the entire VSG (>5000 km, all stages, all future legs to Yamal/KhMAO/Tomsk/Krasnoyarsk/Irkutsk), not a segment-specific design capacity for the 828 km Belogorsk-Khabarovsk bridge. The current ref (neftegaz.ru tech-library 830816) itself makes this explicit: the article structures the 28 bcm/y figure under a top-level 'Характеристики проекта ВСГ' (VSG PROJECT characteristics) block, separate from and above its own 'Стадия 1 проекта ВСГ: строительство газопровода-перемычки' (Stage 1: construction of the bridge pipeline = Belogorsk-Khabarovsk) block, which gives ONLY length (~830 km) and no capacity figure of its own. No source found anywhere states a segment-specific throughput/capacity number for Belogorsk-Khabarovsk. Recommend either removing Capacity/CapacityUnits from this segment-level row (leaving it to a project/system-level record if GEM tracks VSG at that level) or keeping it with an explicit ResearcherNotes caveat that 28 bcm/y is the full multi-thousand-km VSG target, not this bridge's own capacity.
validity.researcher_notes: Read the full neftegaz.ru article structure directly (not just a keyword hit): 'Характеристики проекта ВСГ протяженность: более 5000 км; пропускная мощность - 28 млрд м3/год... ресурсная база - месторождения, зарезервированные для МГП Северный поток 2; маршрут: полуостров Ямал, ХМАО, Томская область, Кемеровская область, Красноярский край и Иркутская область' -- this is explicitly the WHOLE-SYSTEM block. validity.recommendation: FuelSource='Yamal gas fields' is also a whole-VSG-system aggregate (the SAME neftegaz.ru article's system-level block lists 'ресурсная база - месторождения, зарезервированные для МГП Северный поток 2' / route 'полуостров Ямал, ХМАО...' -- gas that would need the yet-unbuilt WESTERN legs of VSG to ever reach this bridge). For the 828 km Belogorsk-Khabarovsk segment specifically, the primary announcement article (interfax.ru) is explicit and direct: 'Эта перемычка по сути свяжет Якутский и Сахалинский центры добычи' (this bridge will in essence connect the Yakutia and Sakhalin production centers) -- i.e. Power of Siberia / Chayanda-Kovykta (Yakutia) gas on one end and Sakhalin-Khabarovsk-Vladivostok (Sakhalin shelf) gas on the other. energypolicy.ru corroborates independently: the segment's purpose is 'соединение в единую газотранспортную систему газопроводов Восточной Сибири и Дальнего Востока' (uniting Eastern Siberia and Far East gas pipeline systems) and gas supply to the Jewish AO, plus acting as a China-contract backup route using 'восточносибирского газа' (Eastern Siberian gas). Recommend correcting FuelSource for this segment to 'Power of Siberia (Chayanda/Kovykta, Yakutia) and Sakhalin gas fields', with a note that Yamal is the aggregate future VSG-system resource base, not what feeds this specific bridge.
validity.researcher_notes: Two independent origins (interfax.ru national wire quoting Gazprom + energypolicy.ru independent academic analysis) agree the segment connects Yakutia (Power of Siberia/Chayanda) and Sakhalin gas, not Yamal.
